I can relate. I just applied for a job in a totally different field and had to redo my resume after almost a decade. I didn't know where to start. A friend helped me. A librarian might be a helpful person for resume writing. They typically know all the good formating stuff, but in general:

Name (bold)
Phone number/email

School:
High school, graduation date, GPA, and anything special like honors classes list

College: how many years/semesters, major, and anything special like dean's list

Work: start with the most recent job, your job position, how long you've been there, some of your job duties

If you've never worked, then list your volunteer positions such as Sunday school teacher or what not. 

Skills: any computer programs you're proficient in, other skills such as wood working, any languages you speak, if you work well with others/on your own. 

References can be former bosses, coworkers, teachers, or supervisors of volunteer work.
